verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp near Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Camp by the sea, right across from Baal Zephon.
Pharaoh will think, 'The people of Israel are wandering around the land in confusion. The desert has closed them in.'

And I will make Pharaoh stubborn, and he will chase after them. But I will win glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD." So the people of Israel did this.

When the king of Egypt was told that the people had run away, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them. They said, "What have we done? We have let the people of Israel go, and now they will not work for us!"
So Pharaoh got his chariot ready and took his army with him.
He took six hundred of his best chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers in charge of all of them.
The LORD made Pharaoh king of Egypt stubborn, and he chased after the people of Israel, who were marching out boldly.
The Egyptians chased after them. All of Pharaoh's horses and chariots, his horsemen and his army, caught up with them as they were camped by the sea near Pi Hahiroth, across from Baal Zephon.
As Pharaoh came near, the people of Israel looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them. They were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
They said to Moses, "Were there no graves in Egypt, so you brought us out here to die in the desert? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
Did we not tell you in Egypt, 'Leave us alone, and let us work for the Egyptians'? It would have been better for us to work for the Egyptians than to die in the desert!"
Moses answered the people, "Do not be afraid. Stand firm, and you will see how the LORD will save you today. The Egyptians you see today, you will never see again.
The LORD will fight for you. You only need to be still."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to me? Tell the people of Israel to move on.
Raise your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea to divide the water, so that the people of Israel can go through the sea on dry ground.
I will make the Egyptians stubborn, and they will go in after them. And I will win glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and his horsemen.
The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I win glory through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen."
Then the angel of God, who had been travelling in front of Israel's army, moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from in front of them and stood behind them.
It came between the army of Egypt and the army of Israel. All night the cloud brought darkness to one side and light to the other side. So neither went near the other all night long.
Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. All that night the LORD pushed the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The water was divided.
The people of Israel went through the middle of the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
The Egyptians chased them and followed them into the middle of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen.
Just before dawn, the LORD looked down from the pillar of fire and cloud at the Egyptian army and threw it into confusion.
He made the wheels of their chariots come off, so that they could hardly drive. And the Egyptians said, "Let us get away from the Israelites! The LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!"
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the water will flow back over the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horsemen."
So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea went back to its normal place. The Egyptians tried to run away from it, but the LORD swept them into the middle of the sea.
The water flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen, the whole army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
But the people of Israel had walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
That day the LORD saved Israel from the power of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead on the seashore.
When the people of Israel saw the great power the LORD had used against the Egyptians, they feared the LORD. And they put their trust in the LORD and in his servant Moses.
